stimulus.text:
“Article II. Each state retains its sovereignty, freedom, and independence, and every power, jurisdiction, and right, which is not by this Confederation expressly delegated to the United States, in Congress assembled.
Article III. The said States hereby severally enter into a firm league of friendship with each other, for their common defence, the security of their liberties, and their mutual and general welfare, binding themselves to assist each other, against all force offered to, or attacks made upon them, or any of them, on account of religion, sovereignty, trade, or any other pretence whatever.”
— Articles of Confederation, adopted by Congress November 15, 1777 (in force March 1, 1781)

stem: Taken together, Articles II and III best explain which later problem of the 1780s?

options.text: Congress could not persuade the states to give up their western land claims to the national government
options.misconception: Background: the states did give up their claims, starting with New York in 1781, Virginia in 1784, and others after.

options.text: Congress could not make a state obey its decisions, since undelegated powers stayed with the states
Congress printed so much paper money that prices rose sharply
options.misconception: The money problem came from Congress having no taxing power, which these two articles do not describe.

options.text: Congress could not keep slavery out of the Northwest Territory
options.misconception: Background: the Northwest Ordinance of 1787 did ban slavery there, so this was not a failure.

rationales.B: Background from the books: Article II keeps every undelegated power with the states, and Article III makes the union a league, so Congress had no power to compel a state that refused to cooperate.
rationales.A: Background: the states did give up their claims, starting with New York in 1781 and Virginia in 1784.
rationales.C: Background: inflation came from printing money without tax revenue, a problem of Article VIII, not of Articles II and III.
rationales.D: Background: the Northwest Ordinance banned slavery north of the Ohio River, so Congress did manage that.
rationales.general:
1. Combine the two articles. Article II keeps undelegated powers with the states.
2. Article III makes the union a league of sovereign states, not a government over them.
3. Background: a league cannot force a member to obey, so a state could ignore Congress.
4. Background: that is why requisitions went unpaid and Congress could not enforce its own decisions.
Remember: when the states kept the powers, Congress kept only the asking.
